prerequisites: Capacity for abstraction: translate from colloquial to mathematical language (and vice versa).
Handle and understand basic mathematical symbology (e.g., summation).
Handle and understand the real function with real variable.
Apply the concept of derivative and integral in one variable to elementary functions.
Use basic knowledge of the applications of the concept of a function limit.
Transform units from one scale to another.
Content from Mathematics II or Mathematics applied to Social Sciences in 2nd year of Baccalaureate.
Content corresponding to Baccalaureate Mathematics subjects.

learning_outcomes.text: Search for information by different means. Manage it.
Make decisions.
Plan, organize, and strategize.
Estimate and schedule work.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.
Be aware of the degree of subjectivity indicated by statistical results interpretations.
Analyze the risk of decisions based on statistical results.
For modeling real problems, an adequate command of oral and written language is very important.
Collect statistical data, present it clearly and summarized, and analyze the results.
Make forecasts for different working conditions and estimate their reliability.
Use statistical models in solving real problems.
Make decisions in an uncertain environment.
Manage the different measurement scales and their possibilities in statistical analysis.
Discriminate between the objectives of a statistical analysis: descriptive and inferential.
Distinguish between a statistical population and a sample from it.
Understand the information provided by a statistical table that orders sample data.
Summarize sample information using measures of central tendency, dispersion, and position.
Compare information obtained from different samples.
Recognize the degree of dependence between different characteristics of a sample.
Model the existing dependence between the different characteristics of the sample using a function (linear or non-linear). Use the model for prediction. Its reliability.
Know the probabilistic basis of Statistical Inference.
Assign statistical models to different real-life behaviors. Identify the different distributions.
Use descriptive classification techniques and obtain information through characteristic parameters of the analyzed sample or population.
Estimate unknown parameters of a population from a sample.
Manage principles and applications of statistical hypothesis tests.
Compare two populations based on their characteristic and unknown parameters.
Formulate real problems in statistical terms (parameter estimation, hypothesis testing,...) and apply Statistical Inference to their resolution.
Be proficient in handling tables, calculators, and statistical packages.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.

syllabus_topics: DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS: Basic concepts: Population and sample. Parameters and statistics. Frequency distributions. Graphical representations. Measures of central tendency, position, and dispersion. Linear regression and correlation. Other types of regression.

PROBABILITY CALCULATION: Events. Concept of probability and properties. Fundamental theorems in probability: Bayes' Theorem. Random variable. Distribution function. Most common probability models in Engineering, their most important characteristics and applications.

STATISTICAL INFERENCE: Point estimation. Interval estimation: confidence coefficient. Construction of confidence intervals for common parameters. Parametric hypothesis testing: Concepts related to hypothesis testing. Non-parametric tests: Chi-square test, goodness-of-fit to a distribution, tests of independence and homogeneity. Normality tests. Inference in regression.
Practice 5: Tests of independence and linear correlation.
teaching_methods: Individual study (research, localization, analysis, manipulation, elaboration and return of information)
Group work (encouraged in classroom practices, laboratory practices and group tutorials)
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary and extraordinary June calls is calculated as: 0.7 x EX + 0.2 x PL + 0.1 x EC. For the extraordinary January call and differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.8 x EX + 0.2 x PL. A minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the course in all cases. In the June extraordinary call, taking any exam implicitly waives the corresponding grade from the ordinary call. If there is doubt about authorship or unauthorized means, a presential defense may be requested.
